title: Getting Around Pula 2026: Your Essential Transport Guide
metaDescription: Navigate Pula 2026 efficiently. Discover direct advice on buses, taxis, ride-sharing, walking, and car rentals for getting around Pula, Croatia. Sharp, local insights.
content:
## Walking is King
Pula's ancient city center, including the Arena, Forum, and old town, is incredibly compact and best explored on foot. Most major sights are within a 15-minute walk. *This sounds convenient, but in practice, navigating the cobblestone streets with luggage often causes problems.* Pack light for walking days.

## Public Buses (Pulapromet)
The Pulapromet bus system offers extensive coverage, connecting the city center with beaches like Verudela, major hotels, and surrounding districts. Purchase tickets at kiosks, on the bus, or via mobile app. They run frequently and reliably.

## Taxis & Ride-Sharing
Local taxis and ride-sharing services like Bolt are readily available throughout Pula. They are ideal for airport transfers, late-night returns, or when time is critical. Expect higher fares during peak tourist season or late hours.

## Car Rental
*Skip car rental unless you plan extensive day trips to Istrian towns or the countryside.* Parking in Pula's city center is scarce, expensive, and often confusing. Traffic during summer can be frustrating, negating any perceived convenience.

## E-Scooters & Bikes
Rental e-scooters and bicycles are available seasonally, mainly near popular tourist zones and beaches. They offer a fun way to cover short distances, but Pula's dedicated cycling infrastructure is still developing, so be aware of traffic.

faq.question: How do I get from Pula Airport (PUY) to the city center?
faq.answer: Direct airport shuttle buses operate frequently, aligning with flight arrivals and departures. Taxis and ride-shares are also readily available for a quicker, albeit more expensive, transfer.

faq.question: Can I use public transport to reach surrounding towns like Rovinj or Poreč?
faq.answer: For intercity travel to places like Rovinj or Poreč, use long-distance bus services from Pula's main bus station. Local Pulapromet buses serve only the Pula metropolitan area.

faq.question: Is it easy to find parking in Pula?
faq.answer: Parking in Pula's city center is challenging. Look for paid parking garages or designated zones outside the immediate core. Street parking is limited and often reserved for residents.

quickAnswer: Pula's historic core is best explored on foot. For broader travel, local buses are efficient and cost-effective, connecting the city center to beaches and key areas. Taxis and ride-shares provide convenience but at a higher cost. Car rental is only justified for day trips outside the city.
